name: SUPARCO
aliases: Pakistan Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission
pay: Entry grade (SPS-7, equivalent to BPS-17) roughly PKR 100,000 to 160,000 a month with allowances; contract research staff lower. Indicative, from recent advertisements.
hiring: Posts advertised on suparco.gov.pk and in national newspapers; written test then interview. Internships for final-year students through the university.
about: Pakistan's space agency operates the PRSS-1 and PakTES satellites and runs the country's largest remote sensing applications group: crop estimation, flood and glacier monitoring, land cover and urban mapping. The largest single employer of Arid geoinformatics graduates.

name: Survey of Pakistan
pay: BPS-16 and BPS-17 posts, roughly PKR 80,000 to 130,000 a month gross with allowances. Indicative.
hiring: Through the Federal Public Service Commission for gazetted posts and departmental advertisements for others; defence-administered.
about: The official mapping authority, responsible for topographic sheets, geodetic control, the national spatial data infrastructure and boundary demarcation. Technical work spans photogrammetry, digital cartography and GNSS.

name: Pakistan Bureau of Statistics
pay: BPS-16 to BPS-17 and project-based contracts, roughly PKR 70,000 to 150,000 a month. Indicative.
hiring: Project posts advertised on the PBS site around census and survey cycles; permanent posts through FPSC.
about: Ran the 2023 digital census with a GIS-based enumeration block frame and now maintains geocoded census and survey data. Hires mapping staff heavily before each census and large survey.

name: NDMA and provincial disaster management authorities
pay: Project pay scales (PPS) and donor-funded contracts, roughly PKR 150,000 to 350,000 a month for specialists. Indicative.
hiring: Contract posts advertised on the NDMA and PDMA sites and on Rozee; often tied to World Bank, ADB or UN-funded projects.
about: The national and provincial authorities that commission flood, landslide, drought and earthquake hazard maps and run the National Emergencies Operation Centre. Demand for GIS staff peaks after every disaster season.

name: The Urban Unit
aliases: Urban Sector Planning and Management Services Unit
pay: Roughly PKR 60,000 to 90,000 a month for fresh graduates, PKR 100,000 to 200,000 for analysts with three to five years. Indicative, from recent postings and alumni.
hiring: Vacancies on the Urban Unit careers page and Rozee; test and interview. One of the few employers that hires GIS graduates in batches.
about: A Punjab government-owned company that delivers GIS for property tax, land use, master plans, urban immovable property surveys and agriculture. It runs one of the largest GIS teams in the country and has absorbed many Arid graduates.

name: Punjab Information Technology Board
pay: Roughly PKR 100,000 to 250,000 a month for developers depending on stack. Indicative.
hiring: Posted on the PITB jobs page; technical test.
about: Builds Punjab's e-government systems, many of which carry a map: land records, health facility mapping, police and complaint dashboards. GIS roles lean towards PostGIS, web mapping and Python.

name: Pakistan Meteorological Department
pay: BPS-17 entry, roughly PKR 90,000 to 130,000 a month gross. Indicative.
hiring: Through FPSC for meteorologist posts; project contracts for the Flood Forecasting Division and climate projects.
about: Runs weather forecasting, the Flood Forecasting Division in Lahore, the drought monitoring centre and satellite reception for Pakistan. Uses satellite rainfall, snow cover and cloud products daily.

name: Pakistan Council of Research in Water Resources
pay: BPS-17 research posts and project contracts, roughly PKR 90,000 to 150,000 a month. Indicative.
hiring: Advertised on the PCRWR site; test and interview.
about: The federal water research body: groundwater mapping, water quality, irrigation efficiency and drought. GIS and remote sensing staff map aquifers, canal command areas and evapotranspiration.

name: Pakistan Agricultural Research Council
pay: BPS-17 scientific officer, roughly PKR 90,000 to 140,000 a month gross. Indicative.
hiring: Advertised on the PARC site and newspapers; test and interview.
about: PARC and its National Agricultural Research Centre use satellite data for crop monitoring, drought, land degradation and climate-smart agriculture, through institutes such as the Climate, Energy and Water Research Institute.

name: Crop Reporting Service, Punjab
pay: BPS-17 posts, roughly PKR 90,000 to 130,000 a month gross; project staff on contract. Indicative.
hiring: Through the Punjab Public Service Commission and departmental project advertisements.
about: Produces Punjab's crop area and yield estimates and has moved to satellite-based acreage estimation with SUPARCO and international partners. Comparable units exist in Sindh and KP. Listed under the Agriculture Department Punjab site; the CRS site itself is often offline.

name: Punjab Land Records Authority
locations: Arazi Record Centres in every tehsil
pay: Contract posts roughly PKR 60,000 to 150,000 a month. Indicative.
hiring: Advertised on the PLRA site and Rozee; linked to cadastral mapping and digitisation projects. Boards of Revenue in Sindh, KP and Balochistan run similar programmes.
about: Maintains Punjab's computerised land records and is digitising cadastral maps (the Punjab cadastre project), one of the biggest GIS data jobs in the country.

name: Development authorities (CDA, LDA, RDA, KDA, PDA)
pay: Contract and regular posts roughly PKR 70,000 to 180,000 a month. Indicative.
hiring: Each authority advertises its own posts; several have GIS cells created under master plan projects.
about: City development authorities hold the master plans, zoning, land use and building control records for the major cities, and have built GIS wings to manage them. Work is urban planning oriented.

name: WAPDA
pay: Regular posts roughly PKR 100,000 to 200,000 a month with allowances; project staff higher. Indicative.
hiring: Advertised on the WAPDA careers page; tests by WAPDA or a testing service.
about: Builds and operates dams and hydropower and runs the Glacier Monitoring Research Centre. GIS and remote sensing staff work on catchment hydrology, reservoir sedimentation, land acquisition and glacier lake monitoring.

name: NESPAK
pay: Roughly PKR 80,000 to 120,000 a month for fresh engineers, PKR 150,000 to 300,000 for specialists. Indicative, from alumni.
hiring: Careers page and newspaper advertisements; also hires through its environment and planning divisions.
about: Pakistan's largest engineering consultancy, with a GIS and remote sensing section serving water, transport, urban and environmental projects at home and in the Gulf and Africa.

name: Geological Survey of Pakistan
pay: BPS-17 entry, roughly PKR 90,000 to 130,000 a month gross. Indicative.
hiring: Through FPSC and departmental advertisements.
about: National geological mapping, mineral exploration and geohazard assessment. Remote sensing staff work on lithological and structural mapping and landslide inventories.

name: Universities with GIS departments
pay: Lecturer (BPS-18 or equivalent) roughly PKR 100,000 to 180,000 a month; research associates on HEC and NRPU projects PKR 50,000 to 120,000. Indicative.
hiring: Advertised on each university's site; lecturer posts need an MS or MPhil, most now prefer a PhD.
about: NUST's IGIS, IST's space science department, Arid's own institute, Peshawar's Centre for GIS, COMSATS, Punjab University's Centre for GIS and others teach and research GIS. Research associate posts on funded projects are the usual first academic job.

name: ICIMOD
aliases: International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development
pay: Regional professional scale paid in US dollars, roughly US$1,500 to 4,000 a month depending on grade; interns receive a stipend. Indicative.
hiring: Careers page with online application; competitive, English, regional candidates from the eight member countries preferred.
about: The Hindu Kush Himalaya research centre, of which Pakistan is a member. Runs SERVIR Hindu Kush Himalaya, glacier and glacial lake monitoring and regional land cover, and has employed many Pakistani remote sensing specialists.

name: IWMI Pakistan
pay: National researcher contracts roughly PKR 150,000 to 400,000 a month; internationally recruited staff on US dollar scales. Indicative.
hiring: Careers page; many Pakistani staff started as interns or research officers in the Lahore office.
about: Water research institute with one of its largest country offices in Lahore, working on irrigation, groundwater, water accounting and flood recovery with remote sensing and GIS at the core.

name: WWF-Pakistan
aliases: World Wide Fund for Nature Pakistan
pay: Roughly PKR 80,000 to 200,000 a month depending on grade and project. Indicative.
hiring: Careers page; project-linked contracts.
about: Pakistan's largest conservation NGO, with a GIS lab mapping forests, mangroves, protected areas and freshwater systems, and running REDD+ and nature-based solutions projects.

name: IUCN Pakistan
aliases: International Union for Conservation of Nature
pay: Consultancies and project posts roughly PKR 120,000 to 300,000 a month. Indicative.
hiring: IUCN global careers portal and consultancy calls.
about: Works on coastal ecosystems, mangrove restoration, protected areas and climate adaptation in Pakistan, frequently through short GIS consultancies.

name: UNDP Pakistan
pay: Service contracts and national personnel: roughly PKR 150,000 to 350,000 a month at junior to mid level; National Officer grades (NO-A and above) start around PKR 400,000. UN Volunteers receive a fixed living allowance. Indicative.
hiring: UNDP jobs portal; UN Volunteers programme for early-career roles.
about: Runs disaster risk, climate, governance and recovery programmes in Pakistan, including GLOF and flood resilience projects that employ GIS and remote sensing specialists.

name: FAO Pakistan
pay: National consultants and personnel services agreements roughly PKR 200,000 to 500,000 a month depending on level. Indicative.
hiring: FAO jobs portal; consultancy calls are frequent and short.
about: Leads crop and land cover mapping, water productivity (WaPOR), locust and flood damage assessment in Pakistan, and has produced national land cover atlases with provincial partners.

name: WFP Pakistan
pay: National staff roughly PKR 180,000 to 450,000 a month by grade. Indicative.
hiring: WFP careers portal; GIS roles usually sit in the VAM or emergency preparedness units.
about: Food security analysis, emergency logistics and resilience programmes, with a mapping unit that produces access, flood and food security maps.

name: iMMAP
pay: Roughly PKR 150,000 to 350,000 a month for national GIS and IM officers. Indicative, from alumni.
hiring: Careers page; expands rapidly after floods and other emergencies.
about: Provides mapping and information management to the humanitarian system in Pakistan, often embedded in UN OCHA and clusters. One of the most common first employers of GIS graduates in the humanitarian sector.

name: IMPACT Initiatives and REACH
pay: National GIS officers roughly PKR 150,000 to 300,000 a month; international roles paid in euros. Indicative.
hiring: Careers page; GIS officers are recruited for each country mission, including Pakistan since the 2022 floods.
about: REACH produces humanitarian assessments, flood extent maps and settlement data for the response community; its GIS officers are known for high output and strong QGIS, R and Python skills.

name: TPL Maps
pay: Roughly PKR 50,000 to 80,000 a month for data roles, PKR 100,000 to 200,000 for engineers. Indicative.
hiring: LinkedIn and Rozee; batch hiring for data production.
about: Pakistan's own digital map provider, producing navigation data, points of interest and location APIs; part of the TPL group with the tracking company TPL Trakker.

name: Farmdar
pay: Roughly PKR 100,000 to 250,000 a month for technical staff; startup equity in some roles. Indicative.
hiring: LinkedIn; small team, takes interns.
about: Uses satellite imagery and machine learning to map crops, estimate yield and monitor fields for growers, sugar mills and banks in Pakistan. The best-known geospatial startup in the country.

name: Telecom operators (Jazz, Telenor, Zong, Ufone) and tower companies
pay: Roughly PKR 80,000 to 150,000 a month for junior engineers, PKR 200,000 and up for senior. Indicative.
hiring: Each operator's careers page and LinkedIn; graduate trainee programmes.
about: Mobile and fibre networks are planned on GIS: coverage, site selection, fibre routes and customer analytics. Telecom is one of the better-paying private employers of GIS graduates.

name: K-Electric
pay: Roughly PKR 80,000 to 200,000 a month. Indicative.
hiring: Careers page and LinkedIn; graduate trainee engineer intake.
about: Karachi's vertically integrated power company runs an enterprise GIS for its distribution network, a model the public distribution companies are following.

name: Power distribution companies (LESCO, IESCO, FESCO, MEPCO, PESCO and others)
pay: Contract and regular posts roughly PKR 70,000 to 180,000 a month. Indicative.
hiring: Each company advertises separately; GIS cells were created under USAID and World Bank distribution projects.
about: The ten public distribution companies and the transmission company have GIS cells that map feeders, transformers and consumers for loss reduction and planning.

name: SNGPL and SSGC (gas utilities)
pay: Roughly PKR 90,000 to 200,000 a month. Indicative.
hiring: Advertised on each company's site; tests through a testing service.
about: Both gas utilities maintain enterprise GIS of their pipeline networks and consumer connections and run periodic recruitment for GIS staff.

name: Oil and gas (OGDCL, PPL, MOL, OMV and service firms)
locations: field locations in Sindh, KP and Balochistan
pay: Among the highest in Pakistan for GIS roles: roughly PKR 150,000 to 400,000 a month. Indicative.
hiring: Company careers pages, often through testing services; competitive.
about: Exploration companies use GIS for lease management, seismic survey planning, pipeline routing and environmental compliance. Hiring is cyclical and competitive.

name: Khatib & Alami
pay: Roughly SAR 6,000 to 15,000 a month in Saudi Arabia for GIS specialists, more for developers; housing often included. Indicative, from alumni.
hiring: Careers portal and LinkedIn; recruits Pakistani GIS professionals directly and through agencies.
about: One of the largest GIS consultancies in the Middle East, delivering enterprise GIS for Saudi and Gulf ministries, municipalities and utilities. A major employer of Pakistani GIS staff in the Gulf.

name: AECOM and global engineering consultancies in the Gulf
pay: Roughly AED or SAR 8,000 to 20,000 a month for analysts to senior analysts. Indicative.
hiring: Global careers portals; giga-projects in Saudi Arabia (NEOM, Red Sea, Diriyah) drive GIS demand.
about: The large engineering firms running Gulf infrastructure and master-planning projects all maintain geospatial teams; AECOM, WSP, Parsons, Jacobs, Dar and Atkins recruit GIS staff from Pakistan regularly.

name: General Authority for Survey and Geospatial Information (GEOSA), Saudi Arabia
pay: Contractor roles roughly SAR 8,000 to 18,000 a month. Indicative.
hiring: Mostly through contractors (Khatib & Alami, Esri Saudi Arabia and others) rather than direct hiring of foreigners.
about: Saudi Arabia's national mapping and geospatial agency, running the national spatial data infrastructure, base mapping and geodetic network, which creates a large contractor market for GIS staff.

name: Esri
pay: Roughly US$70,000 to 130,000 a year in the United States; regional distributors pay local scales. Indicative.
hiring: Esri careers portal; most roles need work authorisation in the country; distributors (Esri Saudi Arabia, Esri UK, Esri India) hire regionally.
about: The maker of ArcGIS. Direct hiring from Pakistan is rare, but Esri's Gulf distributors and partner firms recruit Pakistani staff, and Esri's Young Scholars Award brings students to the User Conference.

name: Planet Labs
pay: Roughly US$90,000 to 160,000 a year in the United States and Europe. Indicative.
hiring: Careers page; some remote roles in Europe; strong Python and machine learning expected.
about: Operates the largest fleet of Earth imaging satellites (PlanetScope and SkySat) with daily global coverage. Its data is used in Pakistan for crop monitoring and flood mapping; hiring is international.

name: Vantor (formerly Maxar Intelligence)
pay: Roughly US$80,000 to 150,000 a year. Indicative.
hiring: Careers page; many US roles require security clearance, international roles are fewer.
about: Maxar Intelligence was renamed Vantor in 2025. It provides WorldView very-high-resolution imagery and 3D terrain products; its open data programme publishes free imagery after major disasters including Pakistan's floods.

name: TomTom and HERE Technologies
pay: Roughly €45,000 to 90,000 a year in the Netherlands and Germany; India offices on local scales. Indicative.
hiring: Careers pages; both have large map production centres in India and recruit globally for engineering.
about: The two largest independent map data companies, supplying navigation and location platforms to car makers and apps. Map production and quality roles value GIS graduates.
